claims.evidence: Photo 0-2 show standard slatted wooden pallets consistent with storage/shipping use.

claims.claim: Everything is clean, dry and sorted, no water added
claims.evidence: No photo shows dryness, cleanliness, or sorting state; 'no water added' is phrasing typically used for weighed perishable goods, not pallets, which is odd here.

claims.claim: Weighed at 500 kg on a certified scale this morning
claims.evidence: No scale, weight ticket, or certification document visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Hidden rot, insect damage, or mold inside the wood
risks.proof: Close-up photos of pallet undersides and cut cross-sections, plus a video tapping the wood for soundness
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly compromised stock, worst case

risks.risk: Unclear whether sale is for a single pallet or the full bulk stack shown in photo 2
risks.proof: Seller confirmation with a photo showing counted/labeled units matching the listing quantity
risks.if_unproven: priced as single unit only, the minimum quantity shown clearly

risks.risk: Unverified weight and treatment claims (dry, no water added, certified 500kg) unusual phrasing for pallets, possible scripted/copy-paste scam language
risks.proof: A photo or video of the actual scale reading with pallets on it, timestamped
risks.if_unproven: priced as standard untreated pallet with no weight premium applied

risks.risk: No visible wood treatment markings (e.g., heat-treatment stamp) for structural/export grade pallets
risks.proof: Close-up photo of any stamped marking (IPPC, HT, KD) on the block or stringer

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the underside/blocks showing construction and any treatment stamps
Video panning around a single pallet showing all four sides and the deck condition
Photo of the actual scale display with pallets on it, timestamped
Clarification and photo confirming exact number of pallets included in this sale
response.reason: The witness confirms the item is a standard wooden pallet, so it can be priced at worst case given unverified condition, treatment, and quantity claims; the mismatched 'no water added' phrasing is a mild credibility flag but not sufficient alone to call fraud.
